title: How far is the snail from where it started?
description: A snail climbs up u centimetres each day and slips down d centimetres each night, for ten days and nights. The distance from the start is written as an expression, and the video asks what happens if d is more than u.
teaching_notes: One idea: one day and night moves the snail by the climb minus the slip, and ten days and nights repeat that move ten times. Watch for students who add the climb and the slip.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of the matchstick steps: one repeated change is worked out once, and it is taken as many times as the pattern repeats.
video_script.substitution: The method of the matchstick steps, where the same two matchsticks are added at every step, with the snail's net move in place of the two matchsticks.
video_script.anchor: a snail on the wall of a deep well, climbing up by day and slipping down by night
video_script.payoff_line: The snail is ten times the bracket u minus d centimetres from the start

final_answer.value: 10(u − d) cm ; if d > u the snail slips down more than it climbs and never reaches the top
final_answer.spoken: ten times the bracket u minus d centimetres, and if d is more than u the snail never reaches the top

never_show: the finished expression before the answer beat
maths_rules: one day and night: up u, down d, net move u - d
10 days and nights: 10 x (u - d) = 10(u - d) cm
if d > u then u - d is negative, so each day and night ends lower than it began
check u = 5, d = 3: 10 x 2 = 20 cm up
check u = 3, d = 5: 10 x (3 - 5) = -20 cm, which is 20 cm lower
video_script.design: One idea: one day and night gives a net move of u minus d, and ten of them make ten times that. Assumes the example of one repeated change taken many times. The well and the snail stay on the stage.

<bookmark mark='s2b'/>The distance from the start is ten times the bracket u minus d, in centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Third, suppose d is more than u. Then u minus d is a negative number.
